guidance022.spoken: Being a child, relative or nominee does not let this website decide inheritance or entitlement. A receipt is not claim approval. Never give a helper your password, PIN or O T P.

guidance026.spoken: Check the nominee’s date of birth privately. Ask the institution whether its minor-nominee requirements apply, then return and choose Yes or No. Do not guess.

guidance028.spoken: Check your statement-visibility choice: nominee names or a Yes/No status. A status indication alone does not verify the particulars.

guidance035.spoken: Consent means the required holders agree to this request. Follow the institution’s own signature or authentication process. A helper must not sign for you or receive your O T P. If anything is unclear, pause before submitting.

guidance036.spoken: Contact details, share, identifier and guardian details are optional under the cited securities framework. Do not invent missing information; ask the institution to explain any conflicting requirement.

guidance037.spoken: Contact the bank’s deceased-account claims team. Ask for its current process for a deceased holder; do not use a new-nomination form.

guidance039.spoken: Contact the institution named on the available statement or passbook. Ask it to identify the account and the team that handles claims first.

guidance040.spoken: Contact the institution’s official branch or service desk to confirm where this account is serviced and what to bring. Do not assume every branch can process it.

guidance041.spoken: Contact the mutual-fund company (A M C) or its record-service provider (R T A). Ask for its current process for a deceased holder; do not use a new-nomination form.

guidance051.spoken: Enter the minor nominee’s date of birth accurately in the official form’s requested format. It is mandatory for a minor nominee under this securities framework. Guardian details are optional under the cited framework; ask the institution to explain its current instructions.

guidance052.spoken: Enter the nominee’s accurate name and relationship to the account holder on the official form. These are mandatory nominee particulars under the cited securities framework.

guidance056.spoken: First check whether a nomination already exists and whether you need to add or change it. Obtain the matching current form or authenticated online workflow.

guidance057.spoken: Follow the bank’s current form for the nominee’s particulars and relationship. Ask the bank to explain any uncertain field.

supportIntro.spoken: Choose one answer. You can ask for help if you are unsure.

unclaimedTask.spoken: Need help with old shares or savings?

complaintTask.spoken: A bank or company has not fixed your problem?

inventoryTask.spoken: What other accounts should I check?

supportBoundary.spoken: This guide helps you prepare. It does not send requests or recover money.

tipsOffer.spoken: A group sent me trading tips

paidOffer.spoken: I already paid or shared access

tipsHelp.spoken: If you borrow to trade, you still owe the money after a loss. A Telegram tip cannot promise profit.

schemeHelp.spoken: Pause if someone promises profit, rushes you to pay, or pays you to recruit others. A copied logo proves nothing.

ipoHelp.spoken: An I P O is a company offering shares. Apply through your bank or a registered service. A payment to a stranger is not proof you will get shares.

riskUnknown.spoken: We have not checked this offer. Even without these warning signs, it may be unsafe.

riskPractice.spoken: Practice: a group promises profit if you borrow and pay today. What would you do?

riskCorrect.spoken: Yes. Check independently before acting. You could still lose money.

riskIncorrect.spoken: A promise does not make this safe. Pause and check. Keep your account access private.

fraudHelp.spoken: Contact your bank now about the payment. Keep messages and payment records. Use the official cybercrime reporting service. Money recovery is not guaranteed.

officialIPO.spoken: How to apply for a new share offer

oldHoldingHelp.spoken: Find the bank or company name on your paper. Start there. You do not need to know the process yet.

oldSharesHelp.spoken: Ask the company where your shares or unpaid dividends are now. Ask whether they moved to I E P F, the fund that holds some unclaimed money and shares.

oldMFHelp.spoken: Ask the mutual-fund company to find the account in its records. Ask about MITRA, a service for finding inactive fund accounts.

oldBankHelp.spoken: Ask the bank to find your deposit and explain how to claim it. A share-market complaint website cannot handle a bank deposit.

iepfLimit.spoken: Ask the company for the current form, documents and contact person. We could not fully check this website; its screens may differ.

officialMITRA.spoken: Read about finding old fund accounts

complaintHelp.spoken: First write to the bank or company. Say what went wrong and what you want fixed. Keep its reply.

securitiesHelp.spoken: First complain to the broker or fund company. If it does not fix the problem, check SCORES, the official securities complaint website.

bankComplaintHelp.spoken: First complain to your bank. If it does not fix the problem, check the Reserve Bank complaint instructions. SCORES is not for bank deposits.

unknownComplaintHelp.spoken: Ask the company which official complaint service applies. Report suspected online fraud through the separate fraud service.

complaintSteps.spoken: Keep the dates, your request and the reply. Use full account numbers only in the official complaint service.

inventoryHelp.spoken: Look at passbooks, deposit receipts and share or fund statements. Check each separate deposit. Add accounts you can identify. Ask about anything uncertain.

handoffTitle.spoken: Can your chosen person use the sheet?

handoffHelp.spoken: Try this with someone you trust. Sharing the sheet does not let them sign or move money for you.

handoffFind.spoken: They can find the sheet and account papers

handoffNext.spoken: They can explain the next step

handoffAccess.spoken: We arranged access without passwords or OTPs on the sheet

handoffDone.spoken: You reported that the person can use the sheet

handoffPending.spoken: The handover has not been checked

reviewHabit.spoken: Check again after an account or family change. This date is your reminder, not a legal deadline. Import the calendar file to get an alert.

restoredReview.spoken: This is a saved copy. Check what has changed. Save again after editing.

timelineHelp.spoken: These notes are private. Leave out full account numbers, I D numbers, passwords and OTPs.

eventContact.spoken: I complained to the bank or company

eventCorrection.spoken: It asked me to correct something

eventEscalate.spoken: I sent an official complaint outside the company

eventResolved.spoken: The problem is fixed, according to me

eventLocation.spoken: Where did you keep the reply or receipt?

timelineLimit.spoken: You can keep twenty events here. Save or download your record before adding more elsewhere.

draftComplaint.spoken: Prepare a letter to follow up

draftWarning.spoken: This letter includes your private notes. Read it before downloading. Add full account numbers only when using the official service.

draftRequest.spoken: Please explain what needs correcting, what I should do next, and how I can check that the problem is fixed.

recordOnly.spoken: These are your notes. We have not checked that a request was sent or accepted.

sourceReviewed.spoken: Guidance checked: four October two thousand and twenty six. Ask the bank or company about current requirements.

oldSharesKind.spoken: Old share certificates or unpaid dividends

plainHomeTitle.spoken: Help your family find the right account papers.

plainHomeIntro.spoken: Start with one account. Check who is named to make a claim after the account holder dies.

plainNomineeMeaning.spoken: That person is called a nominee. Naming them helps the claim process; it does not decide who legally inherits.

plainHomeTypes.spoken: A passbook, deposit receipt or share or fund statement is enough to start.

plainPrivacy.spoken: Do not share passwords, PINs or OTPs.

plainCoachTitle.spoken: Name a person for this account

plainCoachIntro.spoken: We guide you. Your bank or company makes the change.

plainFormHelp.spoken: Ask for the form to add or change a nominee for this account.

plainProvider.spoken: How to do this with your bank or company

plainFormQuestion.spoken: I want to add or change a nominee. Which form should I use for this account?

plainReferenceHelp.spoken: Find the number on your statement. Copy it into the official form and check each character. Do not enter it here.

plainPersonTitle.spoken: Name the person you want to nominate

plainPersonHelp.spoken: On the official form, enter their full name and how they are related to the account holder.

plainPersonQuestion.spoken: Asha owns the account. She wants to nominate Tara, her daughter. Whose name goes in the nominee box?

plainMinorHelp.spoken: Check their date of birth. Ask the bank or company if its child-nominee rules apply. Do not guess.

plainMinorSecurities.spoken: Enter the child’s correct date of birth on the official form. Ask about any other details the company requests.

plainMinorBank.spoken: Ask the bank which birth-date and guardian details its form needs.

plainSubmitHelp.spoken: Check the account, names and consent privately. Send the form through the official service. Keep its receipt.

plainJoint.spoken: If more than one person holds the account, ask how every required holder agrees. A helper must not sign for you.

plainResponseHelp.spoken: Choose the message you actually received. You will check it before changing your record.

plainResponseCorrection.spoken: They asked for a correction or rejected it

plainResponseNotSent.spoken: I have not sent the form

plainReceiptMeaning.spoken: A receipt means the form arrived. It does not mean the nominee was recorded.

plainCorrectionHelp.spoken: Ask for the exact reason in writing. Keep the reply. This is still not a recorded nomination.

plainRecordCorrection.spoken: Record that a correction is needed

plainContinuePerson.spoken: I understand whose details to enter

plainDematMeaning.spoken: Demat: an account that holds shares electronically. The broker or service provider helps you with it.

plainFolioMeaning.spoken: Folio: the account number on a mutual-fund company’s statement.

plainGuardianMeaning.spoken: Guardian: the person responsible for a child. Ask the institution who can act in your case.

plainOldAsk.spoken: Please tell me where this account or these shares are held now, and what I need to do next.

plainComplaintAsk.spoken: This is the problem. Please tell me how you will fix it, or explain what I need to provide.

plainNotSent.spoken: Nothing is sent from this website.

plainRemedy.spoken: What do you want them to fix?

plainIssueHelp.spoken: Optional. Use a short description. Full account or I D numbers are not needed here.

plainCaseDetails.spoken: Describe the problem for your letter

plainLetterReady.spoken: This is a draft to review. Downloading does not send it.

plainFollowupNext.spoken: After sending, keep the receipt. Come back to record the reply and your next follow-up date.

plainEntryHelp.spoken: Look at the name and account type on your paper. It is okay not to know.

plainAccountSetup.spoken: Tell us which account to check

plainHandoffDetails.spoken: Check the handover with your chosen person

plainCheckQuestion.spoken: Is anyone already named for this account?

plainRightsQuestion.spoken: Does naming Tara decide who legally inherits?

plainRightsNo.spoken: No. Naming a nominee helps the claim process. Legal inheritance is a separate matter.

plainRightsWrong.spoken: That is not what nomination does. Naming a person does not decide who legally inherits.

plainPaperBank.spoken: A bank passbook or deposit receipt

plainClaimNext.spoken: Ask the bank or company for the claim steps

plainClaimAsk.spoken: The account holder has died. Which claim process applies, and which documents do I need?

plainClaimReceipt.spoken: A receipt means your request arrived. It is not claim approval.

plainClaimWritten.spoken: Ask for a written document list before travelling or paying for papers.

plainClaimTeam.spoken: Contact the bank or company named on the account paper. Ask for its team that handles claims after a death.

paperNoScript.spoken: If the account guide does not open, use these written steps. No sign-in is needed.

paperBlank.spoken: Write your notes on your own paper. This page does not save or send them.

evidenceLocation.spoken: Where did you keep the institution record? (optional)

evidenceLocationHelp.spoken: Write a place you can find again, such as your blue folder. Keep full account numbers and documents outside this guide.

intendedChecksTitle.spoken: Check the details against your request

intendedAccountCheck.spoken: This is the right account or folio

intendedNamesCheck.spoken: The nominee names and relationships match my request

intendedOtherCheck.spoken: The shares and child details, if any, match my request

intendedCheckHelp.spoken: A Yes status cannot prove the names or other details. Check a record that actually shows them, or ask the institution.

correctionField.spoken: Which field or document needs a correction? (optional)

correctionReason.spoken: What exact reason did they give? (optional)

suppliedEvidence.spoken: Where is the document or corrected copy you sent? (optional)

caseOptional.spoken: Add only the facts needed for your follow-up. These private notes are left out of the family sheet and listening.

eventEntityATR.spoken: I received the company’s report on my SCORES complaint

eventBodyATR.spoken: I received the designated body’s review report

eventFirstReview.spoken: I asked SCORES for first review

eventSecondReview.spoken: I asked SCORES for second review

reviewTitle.spoken: If you disagree with the complaint reply

reviewHelp.spoken: For a securities complaint, SCORES gives one five days from receipt of the company’s report to ask for first review, and one five days from receipt of the designated body’s report for second review. Check the deadline shown in the portal.

reviewReceiptHelp.spoken: Use the date you received that report, not the date you first sent a complaint. A normal company reply is not necessarily a SCORES report.

reviewUnknown.spoken: The report receipt date is not recorded. Check SCORES before deciding whether a review is available.

reviewExpired.spoken: The calculated one five-day window has passed. Check the portal for the current status and available route.

reviewWaiting.spoken: You recorded a review request. Check the portal for its reply; a request does not prove it was accepted.

reviewClosed.spoken: A closed complaint does not prove your problem is fixed. Check the actual action and any available review or dispute route.

removeNoteAsk.spoken: Remove this private follow-up note? Your institution’s record will not change.

openUDGAM.spoken: Open R B I deposit search

tracingInputs.spoken: Enter identifying details only in the official search service. If nothing is found, ask the institution; a negative search is not proof that no holding exists.

tracingFound.spoken: The service found a possible holding

tracingUnable.spoken: I could not complete the search

tracingNext.spoken: Confirm the match and claim steps with the institution. This guide has not verified or recovered the holding.

handoverTry.spoken: Ask your chosen person to try these tasks using the sheet, without your instructions. Record only what they could do.

externalService.spoken: This opens another service. Keep your place here. Enter passwords and full account details only in that service.

publicFallback.spoken: These are preparation steps. The institution makes and confirms any change.

sourceStale.spoken: This route was reviewed more than nine zero days ago. Check current requirements with the institution before using it.
